official.deadline_note: No deadline is published: the programme page states 'Grants you can apply for now: 0'. The last call, for 2024, closed on 3 June and received 191 applications.
official.status_note: The Norwegian government has proposed to end support for the NORPART programme in the 2025 National Budget. This means that only around seven projects will receive funding in the planned allocation in October, based on the NOK 35 million that was allocated to the programme for 2024. Ongoing projects will receive funding in accordance with their agreements, and the page currently lists 'Grants you can apply for now: 0'.
benefits: Institutional grants for long-term academic collaboration and mutual student mobility between Norway and partner countries in the Global South
Increased mobility of students from partner countries to Norway, including mobility in connection with work placements
Increased mobility of students from Norway to partner countries, including mobility in connection with work placements
eligibility: The applicant must be an accredited Norwegian higher education institution
The application must include at least one partner that is an accredited higher education institution in one of the NORPART partner countries
requirements: Applicants must apply through HK-dir's call for applications after confirming eligibility and project criteria
Applications must be submitted in English
application_method: Only accredited Norwegian higher education institutions may apply, and the deadline is set in the call for applications
Applications are submitted through the HK-dir application portal in English
official.application_route: No individual student application route exists; the applicant must be an accredited Norwegian higher education institution that includes at least one accredited partner institution in a NORPART partner country.
official.citizenship_residency: NORPART partner countries: Angola, Bangladesh, Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Colombia, Cuba, Democratic Republic of the Congo, East Timor, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guatemala, Haiti, Indonesia, Kenya, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nicaragua, Niger, Pakistan, Palestine, Peru, Rwanda, Somalia, South Africa (HDIs), South Sudan, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Vietnam, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
official.international_eligibility: Not applicable to individual students - participation is arranged through institutional collaboration projects between a Norwegian institution and a partner-country institution, including master's and PhD students as a target group.
official.description: NORPART, the Norwegian Partnership Programme for Global Academic Cooperation, is an institutional scheme administered by HK-dir and funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It supports long-term academic collaboration and mutual student mobility between higher education institutions in Norway and selected partner countries in the Global South, with target groups of higher education institutions and master's and PhD students in Norway and the partner countries. It is not a scholarship that individual students can apply for.
official.region: Global South partner countries and Norway
official.program_type: Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills institutional collaboration grant, not a student scholarship
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you can apply for. NORPART funds collaboration projects between institutions, and the applicant has to be an accredited Norwegian higher education institution that includes at least one accredited partner institution in a NORPART partner country, so as an individual student there is nothing to submit and no date to diary. The page currently shows no open calls, and HK-dir states that the Norwegian government has proposed to end support for NORPART, with only around seven projects receiving funding in the October allocation from the NOK 35 million that was allocated for 2024. If Bangladesh is your country of interest, it is on the official partner-country list, so the practical route is to ask a Bangladeshi or Norwegian university in your field whether they run a funded NORPART project and can place you through its mobility, rather than applying yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Norwegian and partner-country higher education institutions, plus master's and PhD students who can join mobility that is already funded under a running NORPART project.
application_readiness_checklist: Check with Norwegian or partner-country universities in your field whether an active NORPART project covers your mobility
If you are institutional, confirm that you are an accredited Norwegian higher education institution and identify an accredited partner in a NORPART partner country
Prepare to apply through HK-dir in English when a call for applications is published, following the call's cost and budget rules
Do not budget personal student funding against NORPART, since no per-student amount is published
Use the HK-dir project database to see the projects that were funded in the 2024 round and who to contact
common_rejection_risks: Applying individually as a student, when only accredited Norwegian institutions may apply
Relying on NORPART as your funding source when no calls are open and support is proposed to end
Assuming a partner-country institution can apply on its own, when the application must be led by a Norwegian institution
Using the dead uhr.no URL for current information instead of the HK-dir page
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Unknown from the official page, since no per-student award terms are published; treat any student costs as uncovered unless a host project states otherwise.
document_audit: Institutions apply in English through the HK-dir application portal, as required by the awarding body
Verify the accreditation status of both the Norwegian applicant and the partner institution before applying
Project budgets must follow HK-dir's guidelines for permitted cost categories, which apply mainly to projects allocated from 2024 onwards
alerts: The Norwegian government has proposed to end support for NORPART, so no new award should be assumed in the coming cycles
The page lists 'Grants you can apply for now: 0', confirming there is no open call
Ongoing projects continue to be funded in accordance with their agreements, so existing mobility is protected even though no new project funding is available
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No student submission workflow exists; institutions apply through HK-dir when a call is published, and students join existing projects through their home and host universities.
